slot.brief: Given two explicit functions as sets of pairs or formulas, decide which statements about f∘g, g∘f or injectivity/surjectivity are true.

stem: Let $f:\mathbb R\to[1,\infty)$ and $g:[1,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ be defined by $f(x)=x^2+1$ and $g(x)=\sqrt{x-1}$. Which statement is true?

verdicts.working: For x≥1, (f∘g)(x)=(√(x−1))²+1=x. Also (g∘f)(x)=|x|, f is not one-to-one, and g has range [0,∞).

working:
$(f\circ g)(x)=(\sqrt{x-1})^2+1=x$ for $x\ge1$.\n$(g\circ f)(x)=\sqrt{x^2}=|x|$.\n$f$ is not injective; $g$ has range $[0,\infty)$.

Independent check: For x≥1, (f∘g)(x)=(√(x−1))²+1=x. Also (g∘f)(x)=|x|, f is not one-to-one, and g has range [0,∞).
solution:
For $x\in[1,\infty)$,
$$
(f\circ g)(x)=\left(\sqrt{x-1}\right)^2+1=x.
$$
Thus the stated identity holds for every $x$ in the domain.
